# Player gym scene improvements

**Headline:** Turn the Player gym from a bare ship-tuning testbed into a
thruster-navigation training space by adding indestructible, player-destroying
obstacles and enabling player shooting, while keeping the live ship-tuning
panel.

## Problem statement

The Player gym (`GymPlayer`, listed as **Player** in the gym index) is a
bare-bones ship-tuning testbed: one ship, DOM sliders, no hazards and no
shooting. It cannot be used to practise the core loop of flying while firing.
This work adds a set of **indestructible obstacles** that destroy the player on
contact and enables **player shooting**, turning the scene into a
thruster-navigation training space while keeping the live ship-tuning panel.

## Users

- **Ship tuner / developer** — wants to feel thrust, drift and deceleration
  while weaving through hazards, adjusting sliders live.
  - *User story:* As a ship tuner, I want to practise thrusting around
    obstacles while the tuning panel is on screen, so I can dial in the ship
    feel against real navigation pressure.
- **Player learning the controls** — wants a low-stakes space to learn
  Newtonian thrust and avoidance.
  - *User story:* As a new player, I want a set of solid hazards I must
    navigate around, so that I learn to use my thrusters to avoid crashing.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Player shooting is enabled in the Player gym.** `GymPlayer` advances the
   player through the shared combat core and auto-fires the active weapon(s) in
   the direction of travel via the shared `CombatCoreScene._autoFire` path;
   player bullets render, advance, wrap and expire by lifetime.
   *Verification:* a `GymPlayer` test boots the scene, holds a movement key,
   ticks, and asserts `getPlayerBullets().length > 0` and bullet lifetime
   expiry.
2. **Indestructible obstacles are present.** The scene spawns a deterministic
   set of indestructible obstacles — static walls/barriers plus a small variety
   — positioned so the player must thrust around them to cross the play area.
   *Verification:* a test asserts a non-zero, deterministic obstacle
   count/positions after `create()`.
3. **Obstacles are indestructible by player bullets.** Firing at an obstacle
   never destroys it; the bullet is consumed on impact (assumed behaviour — see
   Open Questions).
   *Verification:* a test places an obstacle and a bullet on a collision course,
   ticks, then asserts the obstacle is still alive and the bullet is gone.
4. **Crashing into an obstacle destroys the player.** Player-body contact with
   any obstacle triggers the shared player-hit lifecycle (explosion VFX, brief
   invulnerability and respawn), consistent with enemy-body collisions; repeated
   contact while invulnerable does not double-hit.
   *Verification:* a test moves the player onto an obstacle, ticks, and asserts
   the player-hit count increments and the ship is invulnerable/respawned.
5. **The ship tuning panel is retained and functional.** The config panel
   (`#gym-config-panel`) remains on screen with all sliders, colour inputs,
   scheme toggle and Save button working alongside the obstacles and shooting.
   *Verification:* the existing panel tests still pass and an explicit
   assertion confirms the panel coexists with obstacles/shooting.
6. **Shared-core reuse and parity are preserved.** Input, auto-fire and
   collision handling are consumed from the shared combat core (no divergent
   copies), and any gym-only divergence (obstacles not present in the shipped
   game) is recorded with a documented reason, per the AGENTS.md gym↔game parity
   convention.
   *Verification:* the repo-wide duplicate-body guard
   (`CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`) and the gym-parity docs assertion pass.
7. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
8. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Shared core first.** Reuse `CombatCoreScene`/`CombatScene` for the player
  control, auto-fire and collision steps; do not re-implement them in the gym
  (AGENTS.md gym-parity convention; enforced by the duplicate-body guard).
- **Obstacles are indestructible** and must not be cleared by player bullets or
  the EXPLODE-style paths.
- **Deterministic for tests** — obstacle positions must be reproducible across
  loads/tests (supports the fixed-layout assumption).
- No new enemies or power-ups are required by this item.
- UK English in all code comments and documentation.

## Existing state

- `src/scenes/gym/GymPlayer.ts` extends `Phaser.Scene` directly. It renders a
  single `Player` ship, polls arrow/WASD input through the shared
  `mapControlInput` helper, and hosts the DOM ship-config panel. It has no
  bullets, no enemies and no collision handling.
- The shared two-tier combat core gives everything needed:
  - `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` — player-control step (`_tickPlayer`),
    the input path (`_readPlayerInput`), auto-fire (`_autoFire`,
    `spawnPlayerBullet`) and shared per-run reset/teardown.
  - `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` — `_handleCollisions` (player bullets vs
    entities, player body vs entity body), the player-hit lifecycle
    (`_hitPlayer`, `onPlayerHit`, invulnerability) and teleport.
- The enemy gyms (`GymEnemies` via `GymFormationScene`) already run a player
  with shooting and collisions through these shared bases.
- `src/entities/Asteroid.ts` demonstrates a roaming, non-firing hazard that
  destroys the player on contact by reusing the shared enemy-body collision
  model — close to the required obstacle semantics but destructible and moving.
- Restart/teardown parity is tracked (AH-0MUII3FYN0072QRT, gap 10); the
  conversion must keep `resetRunState()`/`teardownRunState()` behaviour intact.

## Desired change

- **Re-base `GymPlayer` on the shared combat core** so it inherits the player
  control step, auto-fire and collision/hit handling instead of hand-rolling
  them. The scene supplies its obstacles through the shared participant
  accessors.
- **Add an indestructible obstacle entity** (new `src/entities/Obstacle.ts` or
  equivalent) implementing the structural combat-entity contract, exposed via
  `getEnemyEntities()`, with the player-bullet-vs-obstacle path overridden so
  bullets never destroy it.
- **Add a deterministic obstacle layout** of static walls/barriers plus a small
  variety, sized and placed so the ship must thrust around them.
- **Keep the DOM tuning panel**, back-to-index button and ESC-to-menu
  behaviour.
- **Document** the changed gym behaviour and the parity rationale (obstacles are
  a gym-only training feature, or are made available to the game through the
  same shared code).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/gym/GymPlayer.ts` — re-base onto the shared combat core; spawn the
  obstacle layout; keep the panel and navigation.
- `src/entities/Obstacle.ts` (new) — indestructible obstacle entity satisfying
  the shared combat-entity contract.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymPlayer.test.ts` — shooting, obstacle presence,
  bullet-immunity, crash-destroys-player and panel-coexistence tests.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` / `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` — only
  if a small shared seam is genuinely required; prefer config/hooks over new
  duplication.
- `src/scenes/GymIndex.ts` — only if the entry label/description changes.
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`, `docs/Game Design Document.md`,
  `README.md` — describe the Player gym as a navigation-training scene and
  record the parity decision.

## Related work

- **AH-0MT985FOA008JWM9** – Refactor Enemy Gym Scenes (completed)
- **AH-0MUDYS2SZ004H123** – Asteroids spawn randomly offscreen (completed)
- **AH-0MTD0Z0Y7003T1NT** – Add player to each Enemy Gym scene (completed)
- **AH-0MUD9R3NB0093CBV** – Extract player-hit lifecycle into CombatScene
  (completed)
- **AH-0MUDCT7EU0061OSZ** – Extract shared combat core into standalone gym
  scenes (completed)
- **AH-0MUGZDTFX004RBD1** – gym↔game parity convention (AGENTS.md)
- **AH-0MUII3FYN0072QRT** – gym restart/teardown parity (gap 10)

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MT985FOA008JWM9** – Refactor Enemy Gym Scenes (completed)
- **AH-0MUDYS2SZ004H123** – Asteroids spawn randomly offscreen (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `README.md`
- `docs/Game Design Document.md`
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`

## Risks & mitigations

- **Re-basing `GymPlayer` breaks the tuning panel or restart parity.**
  Mitigation: keep the DOM panel code intact and preserve
  `resetRunState()`/`teardownRunState()` behaviour; the existing restart/teardown
  parity tests must keep passing.
- **Obstacles wrongly require (or duplicate) game code.** Mitigation: implement
  obstacles as a shared, reusable entity and consume the shared collision core;
  if obstacles are intentionally gym-only, record the divergence reason so the
  parity convention is satisfied.
- **Bullet-immunity is implemented by overriding collision handling and drifts
  from the shared path.** Mitigation: prefer a hook/config flag on the shared
  path over a copied collision loop.
- **Layout or visual-style assumption is wrong**, requiring rework.
  Mitigation: the layout is isolated behind a small data table so it can be
  swapped without touching behaviour.
- **Scope creep:** tuning sweeps, additional enemy types, HUD/score, or
  obstacle variants beyond "a small variety" are out of scope. Record extra
  opportunities as linked work items rather than expanding this one.

## Assumptions (pending producer confirmation)

- **Crash outcome** — a crash destroys the player and reuses the existing
  shared player-hit lifecycle (explosion + brief invulnerability + respawn),
  consistent with enemy-body collisions. This follows directly from the item
  description ("will destroy the player if they crash into them").
- **Obstacle layout** — a fixed, hand-designed course (same every load) so a
  learner can practise the same route repeatably. (Open Question 5.)
- **Visual style** — obstacles use the established neon-vector aesthetic with a
  distinct warning colour so hazards are readable. (Open Question 6.)
- **Bullets vs obstacles** — obstacles absorb (destroy) player bullets on
  impact rather than letting them pass through, because they are solid,
  indestructible geometry. (Open Question 7.)

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q (round 1):** Player shooting — add shooting to the existing `GymPlayer`,
  create a new scene, or something else? — **Answer** (producer): "Already
  implemented — no new shooting logic needed." Source: wl comment
  `AH-C0MUB8JD13004UD9E` (2026-09-21). Research: the shared
  `CombatCoreScene._autoFire` path already exists, but `GymPlayer` currently
  extends `Phaser.Scene` and does **not** consume it, so wiring into the shared
  core is still required.
- **Q (round 1):** Obstacles — static walls/barriers, moving obstacles,
  asteroids, or something else? — **Answer** (producer): "Both static
  walls/barriers and a small variety — not many of either type." Source: wl
  comment `AH-C0MUB8JD13004UD9E`.
- **Q (round 1):** Scene purpose and scope / should the ship tuning panel
  remain? — **Answer** (producer): "Include it — the ship tuning controls panel
  should remain on screen." Source: wl comment `AH-C0MUB8JD13004UD9E`.
- **Q (round 1 follow-up):** Crash behaviour — destroyed and respawn (like enemy
  collisions) or something else? — **OPEN QUESTION**, context: not yet answered.
  Interim assumption: destroy + reuse the shared player-hit lifecycle (see
  Assumptions). Source: wl comment `AH-C0MUB8JD13004UD9E`.
- **Q (round 1 follow-up):** Obstacle layout — fixed designed positions or
  randomly generated each load? — **OPEN QUESTION**, context: not yet answered.
  Interim assumption: fixed, hand-designed layout. Source: wl comment
  `AH-C0MUB8JD13004UD9E`.
- **Q (round 1 follow-up):** Visual style — match the existing neon-vector
  aesthetic or be distinct? — **OPEN QUESTION**, context: not yet answered.
  Interim assumption: neon-vector with a distinct warning colour. Source: wl
  comment `AH-C0MUB8JD13004UD9E`.
- **Q (new, round 2):** Do obstacles block/absorb player bullets, or do bullets
  pass through them? — **OPEN QUESTION**, context: the description says
  obstacles cannot be destroyed but is silent on bullet interaction. Interim
  assumption: bullets are absorbed on impact. Source: this intake session.

# Wire the runtime auto-sequencer into the game's wave generation

## Problem statement

The runtime auto-sequencer (`src/core/difficultySequencer.ts`, AH-0MUDIWETP003XC3X) is a standalone pure-core library — nothing in the playable game calls it. Enemy composition is still hard-coded in `src/waves/Formations.ts` (`LEVELS`) and driven through `WaveManager` by `PlayScene`, so every run uses the same fixed waves. This item wires the sequencer into a playable run so wave composition is generated at runtime from a target difficulty curve, behind an opt-in config toggle, with the static campaign preserved as the default and the fallback.

## Users

- As a **player**, when the feature is enabled, enemy waves should follow a difficulty curve so each run ramps up smoothly instead of using identical fixed enemy counts. (Default-off means shipped behaviour is unchanged until enabled.)
- As a **designer**, I want to define the campaign's levels, names, wave counts and per-wave difficulty targets in a CSV config, so I can tune the difficulty ramp and campaign shape without editing `Formations.ts`.

## Decisions confirmed at intake

1. **Opt-in toggle, default off.** Static `LEVELS` remains the shipped default; generated waves only drive the run when the toggle is enabled in config. A follow-on work item covers *mixing* generated and scripted levels within one campaign: **Support mixed generated and scripted levels in a campaign (AH-0MUH7Q6HN0006QPD)** (sibling, `discovered-from`).
2. **Per-level curves with configurable per-level wave counts.** One `sequencer()` call per level; the curve length sets the wave count.
3. **Fully data-driven campaign skeleton.** The curve config also defines the level count and level names (not just targets). The boss is still triggered after the final configured level (existing `WaveManager` behaviour).
4. **CSV-backed config.** A new `src/data/difficulty-curves.csv` is loaded through the existing `configStore`/CSV pipeline (editable in dev via `/api/csv/...`, bundled read-only in production).
5. **Defaults seeded from current calibration.** The baked-in default targets are derived from the current `LEVELS` measured scores (`levelDifficulty`/`enemyDifficulty`) spread non-decreasingly across each level's waves.

## Existing state

- `WaveManager` already accepts injected `LevelDefinition[]` via its constructor and `setLevels()`, defaulting to static `LEVELS`; it owns plan/spawn/progression and the boss trigger.
- `sequencer(curve, candidates, options)` returns one `ShootableWave` per curve entry, each with one adjusted group and a `shootEnabled` flag; `options.defaultShootEnabled` applies to the whole call, which is why generation is done **per level** (so Levels 1–3 and 4–5 can differ).
- `AdjustedGroup` extends `WaveGroup`, so `ShootableWave.groups` maps structurally to `WaveDefinition.groups`.
- Config tunables live in two pipelines: CSV-backed `configStore`/`csv.ts`/Vite plugin (enemies, ship) and the localStorage-backed `rules.ts` (`GameRules`).
- GDD §2.4 — Levels 1–3 do not fire; §2.5 — Levels 4–5 do. §3.2 fixes level themes.

## Desired change

At run start, `PlayScene` reads the config. When the (opt-in) toggle is disabled it uses static `LEVELS` exactly as today. When enabled it builds a `LevelDefinition[]` from the difficulty-curve config by calling `sequencer()` once per configured level with `defaultShootEnabled = levelNumber >= 4`, converts each `ShootableWave` to a `WaveDefinition`, injects the result into `WaveManager`, and drives the run from it. Any empty/degenerate config falls back to static `LEVELS`.

## Constraints

- **Pure core stays pure.** `difficultySequencer.ts` is not modified (read-only call site).
- **Determinism.** Generation must be a pure function of config + candidate pool; no RNG.
- **No behavioural change when the toggle is off.** Existing `WaveManager`/`PlayScene`/campaign tests must pass unchanged.
- **CSV is the source of truth in dev**; production reads the bundled copy; malformed rows must not crash.
- Follow the existing config/CSV patterns (codec, plugin, store) rather than inventing a new persistence path.
- UK English in prose; Markdown in the work item.

## Assumptions

- The global opt-in toggle is a scalar tunable and will live in the existing `GameRules` settings store (`sequencedWavesEnabled`, default `false`); the per-level curve values/targets live in the CSV. Per-level source mixing is deferred to AH-0MUH7Q6HN0006QPD.
- The campaign fire rule is derived from the (1-based) level number: `level <= 3` ⇒ `shootEnabled=false`, `level >= 4` ⇒ `true`. With a data-driven skeleton this applies to any configured levels beyond 5 as firing levels; per-level `shootEnabled` overrides are out of scope.
- "Configurable curve" is satisfied by the CSV-backed config plus the baked-in default; runtime UI editing is AH-0MUGXDVPH005TIZL.

## Acceptance criteria

- **WaveManager accepts injected definitions** — `WaveManager` is driven by generated `LevelDefinition`/`WaveDefinition` data; with no override supplied it uses static `LEVELS` exactly, and existing `WaveManager` tests pass unchanged.
- **Opt-in toggle** — with the toggle disabled (the default) the run uses static `LEVELS` and behaves as today; with it enabled the run uses generated definitions (test asserts both paths). **Superseded (2026-09-28):** the shipped default becomes on with explicit opt-out per AH-0MUJSUTLA006Q8E1 (see Plan update); the original wording is retained for traceability.
- **Runtime generation runs** — at run start, with the toggle enabled, the game builds per-level curves from the curve config and calls `sequencer()` once per level, obtaining a `SequencerResult` per level.
- **CSV-backed, data-driven config** — `src/data/difficulty-curves.csv` defines level number, level name and per-wave targets (curve length ⇒ wave count); it is loaded through the existing CSV/configStore pipeline and is editable in dev / read-only in production. Malformed or missing rows fall back to the baked-in default curve without crashing.
- **Generated waves drive the run** — the groups produced by the sequencer are what `PlayScene` spawns (verified via the spawn plan / `WaveManager.planSpawns()` or a test harness), not the static `LEVELS`.
- **Curve is configurable** — changing the configured/default curve changes the produced wave composition; two distinct curves yield different plans (test asserts this).
- **Campaign fire rule** — generated levels 1–3 have `shootEnabled=false`; levels 4+ have `shootEnabled=true` (test asserts both).
- **Determinism** — generating the campaign twice with the same config and candidate pool yields identical level/wave definitions.
- **Fallback is safe** — an empty/degenerate curve config, an empty curve, or an empty candidate pool falls back to static `LEVELS` and the game does not crash (test covers the fallback).
- **Testing/validation** — new unit/integration tests cover the codec, campaign builder, conversion, fire rule, determinism and fallback, and they are meaningful and passing.
- **Documentation** — all related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- **No regressions** — the full project test suite passes with the new changes (`npm test`).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/core/difficultySequencer.ts` — existing sequencer; read-only call site (`sequencer`, `defaultCandidatePool`, `ShootableWave`, `AdjustedGroup`).
- `src/core/csv.ts` — add a difficulty-curve codec (parse/serialize + validation, mirroring `EnemyConfig`).
- `src/core/configTypes.ts` — add the difficulty-curve row/config types (leaf module, no imports).
- `src/core/configStore.ts` — load `difficulty-curves.csv` through the existing dev/bundled pipeline and expose an accessor.
- `src/core/rules.ts` — add the opt-in `sequencedWavesEnabled` tunable (default `false`) to `GameRules`.
- `src/data/difficulty-curves.csv` — **new** CSV defining levels, names, wave targets (data-driven skeleton).
- `src/waves/sequencedLevels.ts` — **new**: build the curve config/pool and convert `SequencerResult` per level into `LevelDefinition[]` (plus fallback).
- `src/waves/WaveManager.ts` — confirm/verify injected-definition support (minimal or no change).
- `src/waves/Formations.ts` — static `LEVELS`: default/fallback and level metadata source for seeding defaults.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — build + inject the generated campaign at run start when the toggle is enabled.
- Vite CSV plugin / dev write endpoint — extend to serve the new CSV if the existing generic path does not already cover it.
- Test files: `src/core/csv.test.ts`, `src/core/configStore.test.ts`, `src/waves/sequencedLevels.test.ts` (**new**), `src/waves/WaveManager.test.ts`, `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts`.

## Risks & assumptions

- **CSV pipeline scope** — extending the codec/plugin/store is the largest cost; mitigated by mirroring the existing `EnemyConfig` codec/plugin exactly and reusing the generic write endpoint where possible.
- **Default-curve calibration drift** — seeding from measured `LEVELS` scores could diverge from the static campaign if either changes; mitigated by a test asserting the default generated campaign is non-decreasing and stays in 0–100.
- **Fallback correctness** — a partial/degenerate CSV must never produce an unplayable campaign; mitigated by an explicit fallback test and a single guard at the PlayScene boundary.
- **Scope creep** — runtime curve editing (AH-0MUGXDVPH005TIZL) and mixed generated/scripted campaigns (AH-0MUH7Q6HN0006QPD) are explicitly out of scope; extra opportunities are recorded as linked work items rather than absorbed here.
- **Assumption (toggle location)** — the opt-in toggle lives in the `GameRules`/settings store rather than the CSV; revisit only if the producer prefers an all-CSV toggle.

## Out of scope

- Player-state adaptation (adjusting the curve from player performance).
- Runtime curve editing UI (AH-0MUGXDVPH005TIZL).
- Replacing boss / asteroid spawning logic.
- Per-level generated-vs-scripted mixing (AH-0MUH7Q6HN0006QPD) — **now in scope**, generalised to per-wave generation modes by AH-0MUJSUQD8003FSUT (see Plan update).

## Related work

- **Implement runtime auto-sequencer for dynamic difficulty adjustment (AH-0MUDIWETP003XC3X)** — delivered the sequencer this item wires in (`discovered-from`).
- **Support mixed generated and scripted levels in a campaign (AH-0MUH7Q6HN0006QPD)** — follow-on enabled by the opt-in toggle (sibling).
- **Create Dev Utilities gym scene with curve editor and wave preview (AH-0MUGXDVPH005TIZL)** — sibling designer tool; previews curves but does not affect the game.
- **Design a mechanism for calculating how hard an enemy is to survive (AH-0MTZWZ7MC002B01K)** — delivered the `enemyDifficulty`/`levelDifficulty` scorer and campaign calibration that seed the default curve.
- **Config store / CSV pipeline (AH-0MTZWZ9TE009CVUA)** — the persistence pattern the new curve CSV follows.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §2.4/§2.5 fire rules, §3.2 level themes.
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — enemy archetypes/formations.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q (Round 1): Does the generated sequence replace `LEVELS` outright, or sit behind a toggle?**
  - Answer (operator): **(b) opt-in, default off** — shipped behaviour stays unchanged until a designer enables it. Additionally the operator asked for a follow-on work item allowing a campaign to **mix generated and scripted levels**.
  - Source: interactive reply.
  - Follow-up: created **Support mixed generated and scripted levels in a campaign (AH-0MUH7Q6HN0006QPD)**.

- **Q (Round 1): Per-level curves or one whole-run curve?**
  - Answer (operator): **(b) per-level curves with configurable per-level wave counts.**
  - Source: interactive reply.
  - Research: the sequencer takes a single `defaultShootEnabled` for a whole call and returns one group per curve entry — a whole-run curve cannot vary the fire rule by level. Read `src/core/difficultySequencer.ts`.

- **Q (Round 1): Where does the curve (and its override) live?**
  - Answer (operator): **(b) extend the CSV `configStore` with a new difficulty-curve file.**
  - Source: interactive reply.
  - Research: `configStore`/`csv.ts` are CSV-backed and read-only in production; `rules.ts` is the localStorage tunables store. Read `src/core/configStore.ts`, `src/core/csv.ts`.

- **Q (Round 2): When generated mode is enabled, does the campaign skeleton stay fixed?**
  - Answer (operator): **(a) config also defines level count and names — fully data-driven campaign.**
  - Source: interactive reply.
  - Note: boss still triggers after the final configured level via existing `WaveManager` behaviour.

- **Q (Round 2): How editable is the new difficulty-curve CSV?**
  - Answer (operator): **as recommended** — route it through the existing CSV pipeline (editable in dev, bundled read-only in production).
  - Source: interactive reply.

- **Q (Round 2): Where do the default target values come from?**
  - Answer (operator): **as recommended** — seed per-level defaults from the current `LEVELS` measured scores, spread non-decreasingly across waves.
  - Source: interactive reply.
  - Research: `levelDifficulty(LEVELS[i].waves).score` in `src/core/enemyDifficulty.ts`; campaign calibration regression in `src/waves/enemyDifficulty.campaign.test.ts`.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MTCP1CKB00480BD** – Diver jumps on return from dive (completed)
- **AH-0MT7V5UH90023XWR** – Clarify enemy health / one-hit destruction model in GDD (completed)
- **AH-0MU0F1T2H003B4K0** – Swarm are too powerful when shooting (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `README.md` — matched: acceptance, accepts, actual, adjusting, allow (+182 more)
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: accepts, affect, asteroid, auto, back (+161 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: 0mudiwetp003xc3x, actual, archetypes, asserts, asteroid (+155 more)

## Plan update (2026-09-28) — follow-on children

Four follow-on children were attached to this item after its first audit, because the feature is in_review on `dev` but not yet released to `main` and the changes below revise its shipped behaviour. They have now been planned and are ready for implementation in dependency order:

1. Per-wave generation modes: curve-fixed, hand-authored fixed and dynamic runtime regeneration (AH-0MUJSUQD8003FSUT) — open/intake_complete.
2. Curve generator: per-wave generation-mode control with read-only derived difficulty (AH-0MUJSUT8P008UPQM) — blocked by AH-0MUJSUQD8003FSUT.
3. Retune the default difficulty curve and seed campaign for playability (AH-0MUJSUTXI008NP8K) — blocked by AH-0MUJSUQD8003FSUT.
4. Enable sequenced wave generation by default with a mixed-mode initial campaign (AH-0MUJSUTLA006Q8E1) — blocked by AH-0MUJSUQD8003FSUT, AH-0MUJSUT8P008UPQM and AH-0MUJSUTXI008NP8K.

### Superseded decision (recorded, not removed)

**Decision 1 (Opt-in toggle, default off)** and the **Opt-in toggle** acceptance criterion above are superseded by **Enable sequenced wave generation by default with a mixed-mode initial campaign (AH-0MUJSUTLA006Q8E1)**: the shipped default becomes `sequencedWavesEnabled = true` with an explicit opt-out. The criterion above is retained for traceability; the authoritative behaviour is default-on with opt-out, verified by that child, which also updates the README / GDD / design-doc default-off statements.

### Scope reconciliation

**Support mixed generated and scripted levels in a campaign (AH-0MUH7Q6HN0006QPD)** (open/in_review) is superseded and absorbed by (1): its per-level `source` (`generated`/`scripted`) is generalised to a per-wave `generation` (`curve`/`fixed`/`dynamic`) mode, mapping `scripted` → `fixed` and `generated` → `curve`, with the legacy `source` column accepted for backward compatibility. # Support mixed generated and scripted levels in a campaign

## Problem statement

**Wire the runtime auto-sequencer into the game's wave generation (AH-0MUH6LEYY0054E63)** makes the campaign all-or-nothing: with `sequencedWavesEnabled` off every level uses the hand-authored static `LEVELS`, and with it on *every* level is generated from the difficulty-curve config. A designer cannot hand-tune the levels that matter (onboarding, boss lead-in, a specific set-piece) while letting the sequencer ramp the rest. This item lets a single campaign **mix** generated and scripted levels, selected per level.

## Users

- As a **designer**, I want to mark individual levels as generated or scripted, so I can hand-tune onboarding and set-piece levels while the sequencer handles the rest.
- As a **player**, I want the campaign to keep its hand-authored early levels but ramp difficulty in later levels, so each run is both learnable and challenging.
- As a **maintainer**, I want a single, data-driven campaign definition whose generated and scripted sources are explicit and testable, so the two paths cannot silently diverge.

## Decisions confirmed at intake

1. **Selector is an explicit `source` column in `src/data/difficulty-curves.csv`** (`generated` | `scripted`). `source` defaults to `generated` when absent, so the existing 4-column CSV and `defaultDifficultyCurves()` keep working unchanged. For `scripted` rows `targetDifficulty` is optional/ignored (the level's waves come from `LEVELS`, not the curve). A level number must declare one consistent source; rows that disagree are malformed.
2. **Campaign skeleton starts from static `LEVELS`.** The merged campaign contains all static levels 1–5 (used verbatim when a level is `scripted` or unlisted), overrides a level when configured as `generated`, and appends configured generated levels numbered beyond `LEVEL_COUNT` in ascending order. Result is sorted ascending by `level`.
3. **Fallback is per-level.** A `generated` level with an empty/malformed curve (or a `sequencer` throw) falls back to that level's static `LEVELS` definition when one exists; a generated level with no static counterpart (number beyond `LEVEL_COUNT`) is skipped. Whole-campaign fallback to static `LEVELS` only when the candidate pool is empty or the resulting campaign would be empty. No path may yield an unplayable campaign or crash.

## Existing state

- **Campaign builder** — `buildSequencedLevels(rows?, candidates?)` in `src/waves/sequencedLevels.ts` groups `DifficultyCurveRow[]` by level, calls the read-only `sequencer()` once per generated level with `defaultShootEnabled = level >= FIRST_FIRING_LEVEL (4)`, converts `ShootableWave.groups` to `WaveGroup`s and returns `LevelDefinition[]`. On empty/degenerate input or a sequencer throw it returns static `LEVELS` (whole-campaign fallback). It has **no notion of a per-level source**.
- **Config** — `src/data/difficulty-curves.csv` is one row per `(level, wave)` with columns `level,levelName,wave,targetDifficulty`; loaded by `loadDifficultyCurves()` (`src/core/configStore.ts`) through the CSV pipeline (dev `/api/csv/...`, bundled `?raw` in production) with `defaultDifficultyCurves()` computed from the static `LEVELS` calibration as the fallback. Types live in `src/core/configTypes.ts` (`DifficultyCurveRow`); codec/validator in `src/core/csv.ts` (`parseDifficultyCurves` / `serializeDifficultyCurves` / `validateDifficultyCurveRow`). Malformed files fall back wholesale to the computed default curve.
- **Static campaign** — `LEVELS` in `src/waves/Formations.ts`: five `LevelDefinition`s (names, waves, `shootEnabled`). Levels 1–3 do not fire; 4–5 do (GDD §2.4/§2.5).
- **Wiring** — `PlayScene` exposes `resolveCampaignLevels(rules, build)`: toggle off ⇒ static `LEVELS`; toggle on ⇒ `buildSequencedLevels()`, falling back to `LEVELS` on empty/throw. `GameRules.sequencedWavesEnabled` (default `false`) lives in `src/core/rules.ts`. `WaveManager` accepts injected `LevelDefinition[]` and progresses by **array index** — `WaveManager.level` is `index + 1`, so `LevelDefinition.level` is display metadata and the merged array must be ordered ascending.

## Desired change

Extend the campaign builder so each level's source is selectable, and merge the two sources into one ordered `LevelDefinition[]`:

- A level marked **`generated`** is produced by `sequencer()` from that level's curve rows (as today, `shootEnabled` from the level's fire rule).
- A level marked **`scripted`** is taken **byte-for-byte from static `LEVELS`** (its own waves and `shootEnabled`) and is never passed to the sequencer.
- All static levels remain present unless overridden; generated levels beyond the static five are appended. See the confirmed decisions above.

When `sequencedWavesEnabled` is **off**, behaviour is unchanged: static `LEVELS` exactly. Mixed mode is only reachable with the toggle on.

## Acceptance criteria

- **Explicit source selector** — `DifficultyCurveRow`/`parseDifficultyCurves`/`serializeDifficultyCurves`/`validateDifficultyCurveRow` support a `source` field (`generated` | `scripted`) that defaults to `generated` when absent; the existing 4-column CSV and `defaultDifficultyCurves()` still parse and round-trip, and `source` survives a codec round-trip; `targetDifficulty` is required only for `generated` rows (ignored for `scripted` rows), and a level whose rows declare conflicting `source` values is treated as malformed (whole-file fallback to the computed default).
- **Mixed merge** — a config that marks one level scripted and another generated yields a campaign containing both: the scripted level deep-equals the matching static `LEVELS` definition (name, waves, groups, spacing, positions and `shootEnabled`), and the generated level's waves come from `sequencer()`.
- **Campaign skeleton** — all static levels 1–5 are present unless overridden; a configured generated level numbered beyond `LEVEL_COUNT` is appended; the returned array is ordered ascending by `level`.
- **Generated equivalence and determinism** — a generated level inside a mixed campaign is identical to the all-generated builder output for the same curve and candidate pool, and building the same mixed config twice yields identical definitions (no RNG/clock/I-O).
- **Fire rule per source** — generated levels 1–3 have `shootEnabled=false` and 4+ `true`; scripted levels keep `LEVELS`' own flags (test asserts both).
- **Per-level fallback is safe** — a generated level with an empty/malformed curve falls back to its static `LEVELS` definition while the rest of the mixed campaign is preserved; a generated level with no static counterpart is skipped; an empty candidate pool or an empty resulting campaign falls back to static `LEVELS`; none of these crash (test covers each case).
- **Runtime wiring** — with `sequencedWavesEnabled` on and a mixed config, `resolveCampaignLevels`/`PlayScene` run the mixed campaign; with it off they run static `LEVELS` exactly (test asserts both paths).
- **Testing/validation** — new/updated unit and integration tests cover the selector codec, mixed merge, scripted deep-equality, generated equivalence, skeleton ordering, fire rule, determinism and every fallback branch, and they are meaningful and passing.
- **Documentation** — all related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, the README, `docs/Game Design Document.md` and `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` (the new `source` column and mixed-campaign behaviour).
- **No regressions** — the full project test suite must pass with the new changes (`npm test`).

## Constraints

- **Pure core stays pure** — `src/core/difficultySequencer.ts` must not be modified (read-only call site).
- **Determinism** — generation remains a pure function of config + candidate pool; scripted levels are static data.
- **No behavioural change when the toggle is off** — existing `WaveManager`/`PlayScene`/campaign tests pass unchanged.
- **CSV pipeline is the source of truth** — the new field goes through the existing codec/`configStore`/Vite plugin pattern; malformed rows must not crash.
- **Backwards compatibility** — the existing 4-column `difficulty-curves.csv` and `defaultDifficultyCurves()` must keep working unchanged.
- **Ordering** — the merged campaign is ordered ascending by `level` because `WaveManager` progresses by array index.
- UK English in prose; Markdown in the work item.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/waves/sequencedLevels.ts` — per-level source selection and scripted/generated merge; keep the fallback guard.
- `src/waves/sequencedLevels.test.ts` — mixed-campaign tests (source selection, scripted deep-equality, generated equivalence, skeleton ordering, fallback).
- `src/core/configTypes.ts` — add `source: 'generated' | 'scripted'` to `DifficultyCurveRow`.
- `src/core/csv.ts` — extend `DIFFICULTY_CURVE_COLUMN_ORDER`, `parseDifficultyCurves`, `serializeDifficultyCurves` and `validateDifficultyCurveRow` for the optional `source` field.
- `src/data/difficulty-curves.csv` — add the `source` column (all existing rows `generated`).
- `src/core/configStore.ts` — keep `defaultDifficultyCurves()` and `resolveDifficultyCurves()` consistent with the defaulted `source`.
- `src/waves/Formations.ts` — static `LEVELS` referenced as the scripted source (read-only).
- `src/core/rules.ts` — existing `sequencedWavesEnabled` toggle (unchanged).
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — `resolveCampaignLevels` consumes the mixed builder (verify).
- `vite/plugins/configCsvPlugin.ts` — validation for the new optional column.
- Test files: `src/core/csv.test.ts`, `src/core/configStore.test.ts`, `src/data/csv-seed.test.ts`, `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts`.
- Docs: `docs/Game Design Document.md` (§2.4/§2.5), `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` (§9 sequencer), `README.md`.

## Related work

- **Wire the runtime auto-sequencer into the game's wave generation (AH-0MUH6LEYY0054E63)** — the opt-in wiring this builds on; defers mixed campaigns to this item.
- **Implement runtime auto-sequencer for dynamic difficulty adjustment (AH-0MUDIWETP003XC3X)** — delivered `sequencer()`.
- **Campaign builder: config to generated level definitions (AH-0MUITS0VD000DVSV)** — delivered `buildSequencedLevels()` (completed).
- **Difficulty-curve config, codec and CSV loader (AH-0MUITRZZE000OYQE)** — delivered the CSV schema/codec this item extends (completed).
- **Opt-in toggle and PlayScene wiring (AH-0MUITS1SM008GPR9)** — delivered `resolveCampaignLevels`/`sequencedWavesEnabled` (completed).
- **Create Dev Utilities gym scene with curve editor and wave preview (AH-0MUGXDVPH005TIZL)** — designer curve tool; out of scope here.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §2.4/§2.5 fire rules, §3.2 level themes.
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — §9 enemy difficulty scoring / sequencer.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Config-schema churn** — the `source` field changes `DifficultyCurveRow`, the codec and the CSV just defined by AH-0MUITRZZE000OYQE; mitigated by defaulting the field to `generated` so existing rows/tests are unaffected and the 4-column form stays valid.
- **Optional `targetDifficulty` for scripted rows** — validation must require a target only for `generated` rows; a scripted row's target is ignored. Tests must pin both.
- **Level numbering vs display** — `WaveManager.level` is the array index + 1, so appended generated levels display by position, not by their configured `level` number. The merged array is kept ascending; this caveat is documented rather than changing `WaveManager`.
- **Mixed-source rows** — a level whose rows disagree on `source` is malformed; the existing all-or-nothing resolver falls back to the computed default (generated) curve. A test pins this.
- **Scope creep** — runtime curve editing (AH-0MUGXDVPH005TIZL) and any sequencer-algorithm change are out of scope; extra opportunities are recorded as linked work items.
- **Assumption (toggle interaction)** — mixed mode is only active when `sequencedWavesEnabled` is on; when off, static `LEVELS` is used unchanged.
- **Assumption (scripted source is `LEVELS`)** — scripted levels are referenced by level number into static `LEVELS`; no new hand-authored wave data is introduced.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q (Round 1): How should the per-level source selector (generated vs scripted) be declared?**
  - Answer (producer): **(a) explicit `source` column in `src/data/difficulty-curves.csv` (`generated` | `scripted`)**.
  - Source: asynchronous producer reply.
  - Consequence: `DifficultyCurveRow`/codec/validator/CSV gain an optional `source` (default `generated`); `targetDifficulty` becomes optional for `scripted` rows.
- **Q (Round 1): What determines the campaign skeleton and ordering when mixing?**
  - Answer (producer): **(a) start from all static `LEVELS`, override configured levels per source, append generated levels numbered beyond `LEVEL_COUNT`**.
  - Source: asynchronous producer reply.
  - Consequence: levels 1–5 always present; configured generated levels override; extra generated levels appended ascending; array ordered by `level`.
- **Q (Round 1): What is the fallback scope when a generated level has no usable curve?**
  - Answer (producer): **(a) per-level — use that level's static `LEVELS` definition if one exists, otherwise apply a safe guard**.
  - Source: asynchronous producer reply.
  - Consequence: one bad generated level does not discard the rest of the campaign; whole-campaign fallback only for an empty candidate pool or empty result.
- **Assumption (documented, not asked): mixed mode is only active while `sequencedWavesEnabled` is on.** Evidence: `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` reaches `buildSequencedLevels()` only through `resolveCampaignLevels`'s toggle-on branch (AH-0MUITS1SM008GPR9, completed).


## Open questions

- **OPEN QUESTION (non-blocking, for producer):** How should a level marked
  `scripted` but numbered beyond `LEVEL_COUNT` (no matching static `LEVELS`
  definition) be handled? Intake decision 2 only *appends* generated levels
  beyond `LEVEL_COUNT`, so a scripted level 6+ has no source. Assumed safe
  default (documented, pending confirmation): skip it — consistent with a
  generated level that has no static counterpart. This affects only an
  unconfigured edge case; the pinned ACs are implementable without the answer.

## Plan: changelog

- 2026-09-27 — Planned via auto-complete path (effort Small / risk Low;
  approval gate not requested). Clarified AC 1 to pin `targetDifficulty`
  optionality for `scripted` rows and the per-level mixed-source malformed
  rule (both already stated in Decisions/Risks). Recorded one non-blocking
  open question (scripted level beyond `LEVEL_COUNT`). No child items created:
  the item is directly implementable.

- **AH-0MUAYB4R3002ZIZY** – Need juice when the player is destroyed (completed)

# Enable sequenced wave generation by default with a mixed-mode initial campaign

## Goal

As a **player**, the shipped game should use the sequenced/generated wave generation **by default**, with an initial campaign that exercises all three generation modes (`curve`, `fixed`, `dynamic`), so the improved difficulty ramp is what everyone experiences unless a designer opts out.

## Context

This item deliberately **supersedes the parent's default-off decision**. **Wire the runtime auto-sequencer into the game's wave generation (AH-0MUH6LEYY0054E63)** shipped the feature behind `GameRules.sequencedWavesEnabled`, default `false`; this item flips that default and curates the initial campaign. It depends on the generation-mode engine, the curve-generator UI and the retuned default curve.

## Desired behaviour

- Flip the default: `DEFAULT_SEQUENCED_WAVES_ENABLED = true`; `DEFAULT_RULES.sequencedWavesEnabled === true` and `cloneDefaultRules()` agrees.
- A designer can still turn it **off**: persisted `false` must survive `loadRules()` coercion, and offline/shared/config settings must still honour an explicit false.
- The initial shipped campaign (`src/data/difficulty-curves.csv` and, where used, the static `LEVELS` fixed waves) contains **at least one wave of each generation mode**, so out-of-the-box play exercises the full capability.
- Startup must be safe: any malformed/missing curve still falls back to static `LEVELS` and the game remains playable (`resolveCampaignLevels` guarantees this — assert it under the new default).
- Update the parent's stale acceptance criterion (opt-in default-off) and any docs that state the feature is off by default (README, GDD §2.5.1, design doc, `src/core/rules.ts` comment).

## Acceptance Criteria

- `DEFAULT_RULES.sequencedWavesEnabled` is `true`; `cloneDefaultRules()` returns `true`; a fresh, unconfigured run uses generated levels.
- A persisted `false` is honoured (the feature can be disabled) and a persisted/coerced non-boolean falls back to the default.
- The shipped initial campaign includes at least one `curve`, one `fixed` and one `dynamic` wave (asserted by loading the seed config and inspecting modes).
- With the feature on by default, a malformed/missing curve falls back to static `LEVELS` without crashing (test covers startup).
- Existing rules/PlayScene/campaign tests are updated for the new default; the full suite passes.
- Documentation reflects default-on and how to opt out (README and GDD/design doc).

## Dependencies

- Blocked by *Per-wave generation modes…*, *Curve generator: per-wave generation-mode control…* and *Retune the default difficulty curve…*.

## Key Files

- `src/core/rules.ts` — default true, coercion/docs.
- `src/core/rules.test.ts` — default/coercion tests.
- `src/data/difficulty-curves.csv` — mixed-mode seed campaign.
- `src/core/configStore.ts` — `defaultDifficultyCurves()` defaults.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts` — default path.
- `README.md`, `docs/Game Design Document.md`, `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — default-on documentation.
